feed.title: Wits AHEAD · Daily briefing
feed.subtitle: News, research, video and things to read on AI, data and human capability for higher education.
feed.rights: Wits AHEAD Research Group, Wits School of Education, University of the Witwatersrand

entry.title: US universities race to launch AI majors as the count passes 100, nearly double in a year
entry.summary:
More than 100 universities for America don now offer undergraduate degree for artificial intelligence inside computer science department, wey almost double di number from one year ago, according to database wey Northeastern University Center for Inclusive Computing dey keep. Bentley University AI degree don grow from small-small students wen dem launch am for 2024 to almost 100 students dis year, while MIT AI and Decision Making degree, wey start for 2022, be di second most popular course for di university now, wit 354 students wey register. School management say dis rush connect to how students dey worry about job market wey AI don change, and how employers dey look for graduates wey sabi AI; one study wey dem do for May show say just small pass one-third of 66 schools wey dem survey, wey offer AI degree, dey require ethics course.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD work on AI, graduate capability, employability and just transitions, how big and how fast dis change dey happen for Global North, plus di uneven way ethics training dey required, be one marker wey Wits AHEAD fit use to think how African universities suppose design similar AI qualifications wit responsibility, no just as reaction.

WBUR · Public radio news report

entry.title: Study combines AI-TPACK and Freire's critical pedagogy to rethink AI in African STEM curricula
entry.summary:
Two researchers for University of South Africa (UNISA) come up with one framework wey go help bring artificial intelligence (AI) enter STEM subjects (science, technology, engineering and maths) across Africa, as dem combine AI-TPACK model with Paulo Freire critical pedagogy. Dem base di paper on review of wetin oda people don write, no field work, and dem look tools like intelligent tutoring systems, adaptive learning platforms and automatic marking, dem talk say dis fit reduce wahala for classrooms wey too full and no get enough resources. Di paper recommend strategies wey fit di local culture and ethics, wey go address infrastructure gap, teacher capacity and di way-way different situations, so dat AI no go make inequality worse pass wetin dey now.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD work on AI and data analytics for STEM and teacher education, dis paper give one critical framework wey dey rooted for Africa, to weigh AI promise for STEM teaching against di real wahala of infrastructure and teacher capacity for di continent, na warning wey suppose slow down any rush to adopt AI.

Eurasia Journal of Mathematics, Science and Technology Education (University of South Africa) · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: Survey finds most Built Environment students use AI chatbots but African universities still lack formal AI policy
entry.summary:
One survey of Built Environment students, wey dem present for FIG Congress 2026 for Cape Town, show say 74 percent of dem don already dey use AI chatbot for school work, and dem get mostly positive mind about am, but dem talk say dem no get enough guidance from dia school. Di writers, wey dey write from Namibia and Nigeria, talk say na only small-small universities for South Africa, including Wits, University of Cape Town, University of Pretoria and University of Johannesburg, don develop AI guidelines since 2024, while almost 70 percent of universities for America don already get written AI policy. Dem give roadmap for how African universities fit build AI governance wey fit dia own situation.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD pillar on responsible AI, ethics, equity and policy, di fact say plenty African schools still no get formal AI policy, even as students dey use AI chatbot everywhere, show how governance dey lag behind practice; di roadmap wey di paper give fit be good starting point to close dat gap.

FIG Congress 2026 (International Federation of Surveyors), Cape Town · Conference paper (International Federation of Surveyors)

entry.title: WISE and Education Collaborative partner with five African universities on an AI adoption pilot
entry.summary:
WISE (World Innovation Summit for Education) and Ashesi University Education Collaborative don start AI pilot project with five African universities: Bells University of Technology for Nigeria, Botho University for Botswana, KCA University for Kenya, University of Kigali for Rwanda, and Université d'Abomey-Calavi for Benin. From October 2026 reach June 2027, each university go test one project wey fit its own priority, from AI tutors wey match curriculum and adaptive learning tools, to early-warning systems and institutional governance frameworks. The pilot dey build on top one 2025 baseline study of 47 African universities, wey show say AI adoption no dey balance and governance still weak.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD work on responsible AI governance, na rare multi-country trial wey dey test AI tools and institutional policy together across five African universities wey different well well, and e dey give early comparative evidence of wetin responsible AI adoption fit be for real life.

africa.com (WISE and The Education Collaborative, Ashesi University) · International education initiative announcement

entry.title: Early success indicators at a South African university: a data-centric approach to student success
entry.summary:
Philokuhle Majozi and Kgadi Mathabathe, wey dey University of Pretoria, don bring one new framework wey dem call "early success indicators." Di framework dey track data and support wey students go need from before dem register reach di final exam. Dem base di work on interview wey dem do wit academic success coaches, school leaders and data scientists, and di framework dey focus on wetin students dey good for, instead of di old "at risk" early warning system wey dey show wahala.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Dis one give Wits AHEAD predictive analytics work one South African, strength based option wey different from di normal early warning model, and e fit helep dem design support wey go helep students wey dey struggle, no be just to mark dem.

Journal of Student Affairs in Africa · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: Cambridge-led OpRaise report: AI markers favour style over substance in university essays
entry.summary:
Researchers from University of Cambridge, Manchester Metropolitan and Nottingham test three top AI models, one by one and togeda, on 761 undergraduate psychology essay from three UK universities. Di models agree well among demsef, but dem no agree well well with human markers, as dem dey always favour long, complex writing no matter di quality, and dem dey push marks go di middle of di scale.

Why e matter for AHEAD: As Wits AHEAD dey think how AI fit work for assessment, dis strong research wey cover many institutions show say automatic marking still dey favour style pass substance, na warning for Global South universities, wey get bigger class and fewer markers, no to replace human judgement with AI.

University of Cambridge, Manchester Metropolitan University and the University of Nottingham (OpRaise project) · University research report

entry.title: World Bank video: Korea Partnership Facility forum explores AI for education and skills
entry.summary:
YouTube channel of World Bank Group don release one short video about dis year Korea-World Bank Group Partnership Facility forum, where officials from Korea Ministry of Economy and Finance, World Bank specialists, and one KAIST professor talk how AI fit strengthen learning and prepare people for future work. Di Facility dey fund AI and digital skills programmes for education and work systems for developing countries.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Pillar 4, dis one show say international financial institutions dey now see AI skills training as something wey central to graduate employability and just transitions, no be extra ting.

World Bank Group (YouTube) · International financial institution, official video channel

entry.title: Study finds South African universities' AI policies strong on student rules, thin on privacy and staff duties
entry.summary:
One study wey check di generative AI guidelines wey South Africa public universities don publish show say na 46 per cent of di institutions get institution-wide policy wen dem do di research. Where guidelines dey, dem set clear rules for transparency and student accountability, but dem only talk about privacy, data governance and staff accountability small-small, mostly as advice no be binding rule.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Pillar 6, dis one be direct evidence for Wits AHEAD: di authors dey call for harmonised AI guidance wey dem design from scratch to protect privacy, na exactly di responsible AI gap wey di group dey track.

Universal Access in the Information Society · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: Smartphone AI tools help STEM teachers in low-resource African classrooms move beyond chalk and talk, study finds
entry.summary:
One case study wey Universiti Sains Malaysia lead work with ten STEM teachers from Nigeria, Botswana, Ghana, Namibia and Sierra Leone for one hands-on workshop wey use AI tools wey turn voice to picture, block coding for phone, and circuit simulation. Di teachers talk say di tools make hard science ideas easy to show, make students wey no get laptop fit learn coding skills for phone, and make dem fit test circuit safely before dem touch real equipment wey scarce.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Pillar 3, dis one be good evidence say well-chosen, cheap AI tools, no be expensive equipment, be wetin fit change STEM teaching for African classroom wey no get enough resources, from chalk and talk to real inquiry.

ECNU Review of Education · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: Africa must build its own AI and data, not just adopt it, UFS tells QS Africa Forum
entry.summary:
For di QS Africa Forum 2026 wey happen for Addis Ababa, Professor Sam Tshehla, Deputy Vice Chancellor for University of the Free State (UFS), talk for di session about AI imperative and di future of higher education sey African universities must stop to just dey react to AI, make dem build dia own data and systems wey show Africa language, culture and development wahala. E talk sey AI fit help from admission reach teaching and research, but na only if dem invest well-well for digital literacy, governance and ethical rules.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD Pillar 6 work on AI wey dey responsible, ethics, fairness and policy, dis call for Africa to own dia data and systems match wetin Wits AHEAD dey always talk about, say AI governance for Global South suppose come from inside, no be import from outside.

University of the Free State · University report

entry.title: AI exposure linked to 13 percentage point rise in top grades, Berkeley working paper finds
entry.summary:
One working paper by Igor Chirikov of Center for Studies in Higher Education for University of California, Berkeley, check more than 500,000 grades wey dem give from 2018 to 2025 for one big research university. For classes wey get plenty writing and coding work, di A grades increase by 13 percentage points after ChatGPT come out, na like 30 percent pass wetin dey happen for 2022. Di increase big well-well where take-home work dey count more for final grade.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD Pillar 1 work on generative AI for teaching, assessment and integrity, dis study na warning sey higher grades no always mean better learning: di work wey Wits AHEAD dey do to change how dem dey assess student need consider dis same risk for take-home work.

Center for Studies in Higher Education, UC Berkeley · Working paper, University of California, Berkeley (CSHE)

entry.title: Generative AI closes three-quarters of the productivity gap between more and less educated workers, NBER study finds
entry.summary:
One working paper from National Bureau of Economic Research (NBER), wey Guillermo Cruces, Diego Fernández Meijide, Sebastian Galiani, Ramiro H. Gálvez and María Lombardi write, show one experiment wey dem do with 1,174 adults wey do business problem-solving task. Without generative AI, people wey get higher education dey perform pass people wey get lower education with 0.548 standard deviation; but with AI help, di gap drop to 0.139 standard deviation, wey close almost three-quarter of di first gap. Di advantage no stay well-well sotey dem comot di AI tool for one task wey follow.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD Pillar 4 work on human capability, employability and just transitions, dis finding fit two ways: generative AI fit shrink long-time gap for how people dey perform, but di advantage go fade if no dey try well-well, so di way wey dem dey teach students still need build di real capability wey AI just dey support.

National Bureau of Economic Research · Working paper, National Bureau of Economic Research

entry.title: World Bank warns AI's benefits in Africa could bypass the poorest households
entry.summary:
World Bank Africa Economic Update for October 2026, wey dem call 'Building AI Readiness', dey predict say Sub-Saharan Africa economy go grow from 4.1 percent for 2025 reach 4.3 percent for 2026, as developer activity dey rise fast: Nigeria software developer community for GitHub don grow ten times since 2020, and Ghana own don grow almost eight times. Di report talk say AI fit increase productivity and create work for di region, but e say how pipo dey use AI still no balance, e dey concentrate for just few economy, especially Kenya, Nigeria and South Africa. E mention steady light, affordable internet, digital skills and government capacity as tins wey still dey missing for most part of di region.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD Pillar 6 work on AI wey dey responsible, fairness and policy, dis report na clear warning: higher education systems for Global South no fit assume say AI benefit go just come by itself; to build basic digital and institutional capacity still remain di important first step.

World Bank · Intergovernmental regional economic report

entry.title: Critical review finds Ghana's national AI strategy strong on readiness but thin on classroom detail
entry.summary:
One critical policy analysis wey Matthew Nyaaba and nine oda co-author write, build one Education-Centred AI Policy Framework, dem use am check Ghana National Artificial Intelligence Strategy for 2025 to 2035. Di paper see say di strategy dey strong well-well for AI literacy, youth skills and workforce readiness, but e never develop well for teacher agency, teacher training before dem start work, curriculum and assessment guide, how to teach pipo wey speak different language and culture, and how community fit dey part of decision for school level. Di authors talk say Ghana need one plan wey focus on education wey go connect workforce goal to teacher training, curriculum change and protection for learners.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD Pillar 6 work on AI wey dey responsible, ethics, fairness and policy, dis analysis dey useful reminder say national AI strategy for Global South dey often run ahead of di real wahala wey dey classroom, wey must happen first before di strategy fit work well for teacher and student.

arXiv preprint · Preprint (not yet peer-reviewed)

entry.title: US study finds no AI-driven unemployment spike yet for recent graduates
entry.summary:
New working paper from America National Bureau of Economic Research, wey Robert Fairlie and Jane Wu write, check United States work data from June reach August 2026, to see whether generative AI don start to dey increase unemployment for recent university graduates. Dem compare recent graduates with older graduates and young pipo wey no go university, and dem no see any big increase for unemployment wey connect to AI for summer 2026, even though wider measure wey include pipo wey don tire to dey look for work add almost two percentage points to recent graduates unemployment rate.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD Pillar 4 work on human capability, employability and just transition, na early, data-based check on fear wey say generative AI don already dey kill graduate jobs, e remind us say make we check local tins with evidence, no be headlines.

National Bureau of Economic Research · Economic research working paper

entry.title: Fort Hare study proposes Big Data framework to improve student retention in South Africa
entry.summary:
New study wey dem publish for South African Journal of Information Management, wey Ganizani Mainoti and Roxanne Piderit from University of Fort Hare write, interview staff tirty wey dey work for four public universities for South Africa, and dem check retention report and policy. Dem see say data systems scatter and staff no sabi data well, and dem propose Big Data framework wey dey stand on ethical data governance, data wey dem combine, predictive analytics and personal support, so universities fit stop just to dey react to student wey dey drop out, make dem prevent am instead.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD Pillar 2 work on AI and predictive analytics for student success, retention and early warning, na local example wey pass peer review, e show wetin integrated data system and governance need to make dis kind analytics work.

University of Fort Hare, published in the South African Journal of Information Management · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: World Bank's 2026 World Development Report: AI needs reliable power, internet and skills to help developing countries
entry.summary:
World Bank World Development Report 2026, wey dem call 'The Promise of Artificial Intelligence', dey lay strategy of adopt, adapt and advance for the 5.6 billion pipo wey dey live for low and middle income countries. E talk say developing countries no need to build dia own big AI models, but just to import AI tools no go helep: AI dey work well pass where infrastructure, like light and connectivity, and school system don already dey reliable, while 'small AI' wey dem send with text message or basic phone fit reach pipo where dis one no dey.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD Pillar 6 work on responsible AI, ethics, fairness and policy, dis warning wey the report give, say AI benefit dey depend on reliable infrastructure and school system, no be just access to the tech, dey talk direct to the kind condition wey universities and government for Global South still need to build.

World Bank · Intergovernmental flagship report

entry.title: UCT video: Cape Town summit brings the global debate on AI and universities to Africa
entry.summary:
For one video wey dem release before di Times Higher Education summit, University of Cape Town announce say dis gathering, wey dem co-host wit University of Bristol from 29 September to 1 October 2026, go be di first time dem go hold am for Africa, e dey bring university leaders and policy makers together to discuss AI, future of work, inequality and di purpose of universities. Vice-chancellor, Professor Mosa Moshabela, talk say di summit na chance for African universities to help shape di global agenda, wey show im vision for UCT to push teaching, research and impact for society, while e dey strengthen innovation and entrepreneurship for Africa, wey dey based for ubuntu.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD Pillar 4 work on graduate capability, employability and just transitions, dis one dey remind us say African universities don dey help set, no be just follow, di global agenda on how higher education suppose respond to how AI dey affect work and opportunity.

University of Cape Town (YouTube) · University video

entry.title: UNESCO working paper maps AI use across 200 Latin American and Caribbean universities

category.term: 19 countries, Latin America and the Caribbean

entry.summary:
New working paper from UNESCO International Institute for Higher Education in Latin America and the Caribbean (IESALC), wey dem do wit United Nations University Institute for the Advanced Study of Sustainability, show how AI dey used for 200 higher education institutions for 19 kontri for Latin America and Caribbean, wey dem survey between August and October 2025. E dey look five area, teaching and learning, research, community work, administration and governance, to show where AI dey already, how dem dey manage am, wetin institution fit do and di gap wey still dey. Di writers want say di findings go help institution leaders and kontri policy makers put AI for use well-well, wit responsibility, ethics and make everybody dey included.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD Pillar 5 work on analytics and data for education systems and decision-making, dis one give rare region-wide evidence on how universities dey govern and put resource for AI adoption, one comparison point for South Africa own institution policies.

UNESCO International Institute for Higher Education in Latin America and the Caribbean (IESALC), with UNU-IAS · Intergovernmental working paper

entry.title: MIT's own AI committee calls generative AI 'not an optional exercise' for teaching
entry.summary:
MIT own special committee on AI for teaching, learning and research training, wey di school leaders give di work for January 2026, release dia final report on 25 August 2026, dem describe generative AI as force wey get 'extraordinary potential and disturbing risk' wey university no fit treat as optional wahala. Instead of one rule for everybody, di committee recommend say every department and lecturer suppose set dia own clear rule on when students must, fit, or no fit use AI, redesign assessment and learning goal around am, and continue to dey review dia approach as di technology dey change. President Sally Kornbluth call di report one watershed moment, no be just for MIT, but for higher education generally.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD Pillar 1 work on generative AI for higher education, say big research university like dis get dis kain conclusion from dia own committee dey strengthen di case for Wits and dia mates to treat course-level AI policy and assessment redesign as urgent, no be optional.

Massachusetts Institute of Technology · University committee report

entry.title: New dashboard design principles aim to stop learning-analytics tools overstating what they can tell teachers
entry.summary:
Researchers dem introduce TopoLA, one dashboard wey dey use topological data-analysis method wey dem call zigzag persistent homology for learning-management-system data, to track how one class learning activity dey change as time dey go. Because dis analysis method no get settled rule for how to interpret am, di authors set three design principle for any kain dashboard like dis: separate raw measurement from how you go interpret am, show result step by step instead of all at once, and talk di method uncertainty openly instead of make e look like e too correct.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD Pillar 2 work on predictive and learning analytics for student success, dis one dey remind us say dashboard wey look precise no mean say e dey trustworthy, one difference wey matter well-well for how dem go design and explain early-warning and retention tools to di lecturer wey dey depend on dem.

arXiv (preprint, accepted at IADIS International Conference Information Systems 2026) · Peer-reviewed conference paper

entry.title: Study finds six AI chatbots give African computing students patchy, often Western-centric career advice

category.term: Ten African countries (study); United States (authors, Florida International University)

entry.summary:
Researchers for Florida International University test six big AI language model, ChatGPT-4, DeepSeek, Gemini, Claude 3.5, Llama 3, and Mistral AI, to see how dem dey describe entry-level computer job for ten African country, dem check 60 answer against Computing Curricula 2020 framework. Di chatbot dem dey cover technical skill like cloud computing and programming well, but dem score only 35.4 percent average for how dem sabi local tin like tech ecosystem, language, and government policy; di open-source Llama (4.47 out of 5) and DeepSeek (4.25) perform better pass di proprietary ChatGPT-4 (3.90) and Claude (3.46), while di open-source Mistral AI score 0.00 out of 4.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD Pillar 4 work on graduate capability and employability, dis one be direct evidence say di AI career advice wey African students dey increasingly use fit carry Western-centred idea about infrastructure and job market, wey make di authors talk say dem need more context-based, Ubuntu-style, human-supported career guidance for Global South.

arXiv (preprint; submitted to Computers & Education Open) · Preprint (not yet peer-reviewed)

entry.title: Survey of 443 computing students finds the impostor phenomenon, not confidence, shapes how harshly they judge AI use as cheating
entry.summary:
One survey wey dem do for 443 undergraduate students wey dey do computer science course for entry and mid level for one university for America, ask dem to rate how serious thirteen cheating scenario be, join measurement of self-confidence and wetin dem call impostor phenomenon, di feeling say you no deserve your own success. Students wey get dis feeling well-well, dem dey more likely to rate AI-related scenario as serious cheating, while self-confidence and dis feeling dey show negative relationship to each other.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Na useful evidence for Wits AHEAD Pillar 1 work on generative AI and assessment integrity: how serious student judge AI use fit tell more about dia own confidence and sense of belonging pass di act itself, and dis one matter well-well for how people go dey frame academic integrity conversation and policy.

arXiv (preprint) · Preprint (not yet peer-reviewed)

entry.title: Study of 30,000 student programming submissions finds AI-code matches rising over time, but says that alone cannot prove cheating
entry.summary:
One new study wey check 29,970 student submissions for Python lab work from 2021, 2023 and 2025, and compare dem with 90,000 solutions wey three big AI language model generate, dey show say student code dey resemble AI-generated solution more and more as time dey go, even work wey pass every hidden test. For functions wey dem specify well-well, di models just converge to small number of exact code pattern, but for open-ended task, both student and AI code still dey different-different. Di researchers conclude say dis kain match fit help track change for di whole class, but e no fit alone prove say one particular student use AI.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD Pillar 1 work on generative AI, assessment and integrity, dis one na warning against using code-similarity match as proof say individual student do wrong, and e dey point go di side of redesigning assessment task and building reference solution bank, instead of to just depend on detection alone.

arXiv (preprint, accepted Koli Calling 2026) · Working paper (arXiv preprint, accepted Koli Calling 2026)

entry.title: Wits and UJ researchers show early-warning systems for disengaged students are often tested unfairly
entry.summary:
Researchers from University of the Witwatersrand and University of Johannesburg, for one early paper wey dem never review yet, show say early-warning system wey dey find students wey dey disengage from study dey often test with information wey no go dey available for real as dem dey make di prediction, and dis one dey make di system look better pass how e go be for real use. As dem test three prediction methods on 49,329 weekly, real-time predictions wey come from Moodle learning system records, dem find out say no single method win for every measure, and say if dem lower di alert level, e go catch more students wey dey risk but e go also increase false alarm wey staff go need handle.

Why e matter for AHEAD: This one important for Wits AHEAD Pillar 2 work on predictive analytics for student success because e give South African universities one more honest way to check, before dem go depend on am, if early-warning system go really help catch students wey dey disengage on time, no be just how e dey look after everything don happen.

arXiv (preprint) · Preprint (not yet peer-reviewed)

entry.title: Generative AI access does not mean equal use, study of Chinese, Japanese and Mongolian students finds
entry.summary:
One study wey compare 42 undergraduate students, one university each for China, Japan and Mongolia, find out say just to get access to generative AI no mean say e go useful for study for everybody the same way. Researchers from University of Osaka, University of Minnesota, Waseda University and Kyoto University talk say China students dey switch between local and global AI tools, Japan students dey mostly use global tools for Japanese language, while Mongolia students dey often switch go English when the answer for Mongolian language look weak; all three groups dey also check accuracy, privacy, how much dem dey depend on am, and how e dey affect dia own thinking before dem go trust an answer.

Why e matter for AHEAD: This one na warning for Wits AHEAD Pillar 1 work on generative AI for higher education: language and local technical condition, no be access alone, na im dey decide if generative AI dey really help students learn, lesson wey apply directly to university systems wey get plenty language, wey no be English be di main one, across the Global South.

arXiv (preprint) · Preprint (not yet peer-reviewed)

entry.title: Kyoto University framework offers universities a safer way to share student data with researchers
entry.summary:
Researchers from Kyoto University propose ReLEAF, one framework wey go make universities and online learning platforms fit share di learning data wey dem collect with outside researchers, while dem dey protect student privacy well well. E first give researchers safe fake data wey dem fit use explore, before dem go give controlled access to real data only after dem agree one specific research need with di institution wey hold di data. Dem design and test dis one through plenty rounds of work with data custodians, researchers and students for Japan universities.

Why e matter for AHEAD: This one important for Wits AHEAD Pillar 5 work on analytics and data for education systems because plenty universities, including for Global South, get rich student data but dem no get safe process wey everybody agree to share am with researchers; dis one give practical example wey institutions fit adapt.

arXiv (preprint) · Preprint (not yet peer-reviewed)

entry.title: UNESCO opens global consultation on governing AI so that education remains a common good
entry.summary:
UNESCO don open one global discussion wey go run reach November 2026, dem dey invite academics and policy people make dem comment on some background papers wey dey talk about how to govern AI inside education. Di main paper, wey dem release before Digital Learning Week 2026, show six ways wey education purpose fit spoil if dem no govern how AI dey used, and e talk say education suppose remain something wey belong to everybody, instead of leave di governing to AI companies.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Dis discussion go shape how UNESCO go guide ministries and universities for future, dis na why e important for Wits AHEAD pillar wey dey cover responsible AI, ethics, equity and policy, especially for institutions for Global South wey no get plenty capacity to write dia own AI governance framework.

UNESCO · Intergovernmental body, consultation paper

entry.title: Simple digital markers could flag at-risk first-year computer science students by week five, Southern African study finds
entry.summary:
Wen researchers check four batch of year-one computer science students for one big public university for sub-Saharan Africa, dem see say if you combine one score wey show how student dey push for im studies, with simple background info and just weda di student don log in to di course online learning system before, e fit correctly show 87 percent of students wey go later fail. Di researchers talk say di model simple well well, so dem fit use am as early-warning system from week five of term.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Dis kind simple, low-data early-warning tool fit universities wey no get plenty data infrastructure, and e dey push forward Wits AHEAD pillar for AI and predictive analytics for student success for places wey no get plenty resources.

arXiv (preprint) · Preprint (not yet peer-reviewed)

entry.title: Nigerian study finds male pre-service STEM teachers report higher AI literacy than female peers
entry.summary:
One study wey dem do for 541 students wey dey train to become STEM teachers for Lagos State University, wey dem publish inside STEM Education journal, show say di students rate dia sef AI knowledge well well, and say how dem understand AI fit tell weda dem go use am well for teaching. Di study also see one gender gap wey show clear well: male trainee teachers rate dia AI knowledge pass dia female colleagues.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Dis gap dey important for teacher-training programmes across di Global South, wey want make AI knowledge spread equal for di next generation of STEM teachers, na wetin Wits AHEAD dey focus on for di pillar wey dey cover AI and analytics for STEM and teacher education.

STEM Education (AIMS Press) · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: Universities in Korea, Singapore and the United Kingdom take different paths to redesign teaching for AI

category.term: Korea, Singapore and the United Kingdom

entry.summary:
The Korea Times report say Korean universities don add more than 4,000 slots for AI and semiconductor related courses since 2024, and say application to AI departments for twenty big universities rise by 16% dis year, as government don cap new advanced technology slots to 434 for 2027 because dem no get enough staff and facilities. Di same report compare dis expansion to Nanyang Technological University for Singapore, wey dey plan to put AI inside 40% of dia degree courses by 2030, and to King's College London and London School of Economics, wey dey redesign how dem dey assess students and dey give students and staff license to use AI tools instead of go back to hand written exams.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD pillar wey dey focus on generative AI for higher education, dis comparison show two different way to handle di same pressure, to build more AI capacity or to redesign wetin and how dem dey assess students, one choice wey South African universities sef dey weigh for di same time.

The Korea Times · Established national press, first instalment of a three-part series

entry.title: Study proposes voice-based AI interviews as a richer alternative to end-of-semester course surveys
entry.summary:
Researchers from Technical University of Munich and MIT Sloan School of Management dey propose say make dem replace written end of semester course survey wit structured interview wey one voice AI agent go conduct, wey fit ask follow up questions wia written form no fit ask. One technical pilot for Technical University of Munich show say phone based AI interview dey possible, and di researchers dey plan now one full field study for one MIT Sloan course wit about 60 students, dem go score di feedback based on how specific, how rich di theme be, how constructive di tone be, and how deep di context be.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD pillar wey dey focus on generative AI for higher education, dis study show one practical way to use conversational AI inside teaching: to turn weak feedback wey few people dey respond to into one wey detailed well well, wey lecturers and institutions fit use take action.

Technical University of Munich and the MIT Sloan School of Management, posted to arXiv · Preprint (not yet peer-reviewed)

entry.title: Eduvos academic leader tells CNBC Africa that equal access to AI, not only AI literacy, will decide graduate employability
entry.summary:
For one AI summit wey CNBC Africa organize, one academic leader from Eduvos, private higher institution, talk say South African universities no fit wait again to decide wetin artificial intelligence mean for teaching and students, and say AI literacy, wey mean say you know wen to lean on AI and wen to think for yourself, dey important now like basic academic skills. Di leader warn say access to AI no be only access to degree: if students from poor background no get device, digital support and infrastructure, AI fit increase inequality instead to reduce am among graduates wey dey enter job market.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD pillar wey dey focus on graduate capability, employability and just transitions, dis interview dey remind us say how ready South African higher education be for AI depend well well on equal access to tools and infrastructure, just as e depend on teaching AI skills.

CNBC Africa · Broadcast interview, major African business channel

entry.title: Seven-country study finds universities at very different stages of AI readiness
entry.summary:
One study wey dem do for seven kontris by WISE and Institute of International Education find out say universities dey different stages well well for how dem ready for generative AI, as policy, student attitude and infrastructure no balance. For one private university for Ghana, 64 percent of lecturers talk say dem get clear AI policy, against 27 percent for one public research university, even though 89 percent of lecturers wey dem survey don already use AI demsef before. Di researchers warn say, because big AI models dey learn mainly from English and oda languages wey strong, African and oda Global South institutions fit remain pipo wey just dey use AI, instead of pipo wey dey build am.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD pillar wey dey focus on responsible AI, ethics, equity and policy, di study show say di gap for readiness between institutions, no be only between kontris, fit make inequality grow pass how e dey reduce am for how higher education dey adopt AI.

WISE and the Institute of International Education (IIE), reported by University World News · Established higher education press, reporting a WISE/IIE policy brief

entry.title: Dutch minister calls AI-written theses 'fraud', universities say detection scores cannot prove it
entry.summary:
One Dutch TV station check hundreds of recent master thesis for twelve universities and find out say for almost one out of five, chatbots like ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini write pass wetin di student write. Education minister, Rianne Letschert, call dis one fraud, but di body wey represent Dutch universities, Universiteiten van Nederland, talk say detection score alone no fit prove say person cheat, and say di real question na how dem design di assessment. Delft, Utrecht and Leiden don restrict or ban AI detection tools for student work, dem talk say di tools no dey reliable.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD pillar wey dey focus on generative AI for higher education, dis matter show how academic integrity wahala fit turn political sharp sharp once minister enter, and why di group dey push for make dem redesign assessment instead of depend on detection software.

Times Higher Education · Established higher education press

entry.title: Russell Group students say they are taught little about AI, Bett UK survey finds
entry.summary:
One Bett UK survey wey dem do for more than 1,000 UK undergraduate students find out say 77 percent of students for Russell Group universities talk say dem no dey teach dem much or nothing about AI, against 64 percent for post-1992 universities. Di same survey find out say 78 percent of students go like one degree wey technology personalize and wey go take shorter time, but na only 34 percent feel say dia university dey straight with dem about real work prospects after graduation. Russell Group talk say dia members dey redesign curriculum and assessment rules because of dis.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD pillar wey dey focus on generative AI for higher education, di finding say research heavy universities no teach AI skills well well like oda institutions dey raise straight equity question: which kain graduates go enter job market wey AI don change well prepared.

Times Higher Education · Established higher education press

entry.title: New framework guides statistics and data science educators on teaching responsible generative AI use
entry.summary:
Team of statistics and data science teachers release one framework wey get four parts, understanding, development, reporting and safety, to guide how lecturers go teach students to use generative AI tool well well for coding and statistics work. Dem don improve am through workshop and feedback from students, and dem don already use am for one free online course and for undergraduate and postgraduate teaching.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Pillar 3, AI and analytics for STEM and teacher education, need framework wey ready for classroom, no be policy statement alone; dis one give Wits AHEAD one working model to teach generative AI literacy inside number-based subject.

arXiv · Preprint (not yet peer-reviewed)

entry.title: New tool scrambles assignment images so AI reading systems fail, but people can still read them
entry.summary:
Some researchers build AIRRI, one tool wey dey change how image of printed assignment dey look, dem dey use spacing, opacity and noise plus adversarial attacks, so that OCR tools and AI chatbot go hard to read di work well well, but human eye fit still read am well. Dem test am against three reading system, and di strongest attack push one system error rate from 2.3% go 100%, and anoda one word error rate from 24.9% go 96.7%. Di team also release dataset of higher education assignment to test di method.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Pillar 1, na generative AI for higher education: teaching, assessment, integrity, need protection wey dey work for di assignment level itself; Wits AHEAD dey watch tool like dis to see if integrity fit dey build inside course material instead of dem go dey chase am afta di fact.

arXiv · Preprint (not yet peer-reviewed)

entry.title: New framework argues the cost of AI essay-marking systems should be measured against trustworthy scores, not efficiency alone
entry.summary:
New paper propose “Cost-Aware Measurement Design” framework for automated essay-scoring systems, e argue say di computing cost of AI marking na wetin pipo dey normally treat as simple technical efficiency matter, but e be measurement-design choice for real. Di framework define “cost per defensible score” wey dey compare scoring systems only among designs wey meet minimum standard of trustworthy measurement, e dey treat institution governance and oversight capacity as limit on which design dem fit use, no be price wey dem go reduce.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD pillar on generative AI for higher education, teaching, assessment and integrity, dis framework give universities wey dey consider AI-assisted marking one concrete way to ask whether cheaper system dey really produce score wey dem fit defend, instead of dem to judge automated assessment tools only by speed and cost.

arXiv (preprint) · Preprint (not yet peer-reviewed)

entry.title: Study of a South African university finds online “participation profiles” mostly track how long a learner is observed, not how engaged they are
entry.summary:
Afta dem analyse 16,448 student-course records from 4,599 students for 152 courses for one South African public university, researchers test eight measures wey pipo dey normally use for online “participation”, dem see say all of dem dey show how long dem observe student for course pass how di student really dey participate. Afta dem adjust dis one, small set of measures still dey group students into one broad two-profile pattern and one more detailed four-profile pattern, but di confidence no too strong.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD pillar on AI and predictive analytics for student success, dis finding be direct warning for early-warning and retention systems wey dem build with South African data: unless dem account for how long dem dey track student, profile wey dem mark as “no dey participate” fit just be student wey dem observe for short time, no be person wey really dey for risk.

arXiv (preprint) · Preprint (not yet peer-reviewed)
